evals.prompt: Design an M3 web incident dashboard with a list and incident details, usable on phones and desktops. Give a design specification only.
evals.expected_output: Use list-detail adaptation, semantic roles, action hierarchy, loading/empty/error states and accessible interactions. Do not edit app code or install dependencies.

evals.prompt: Our React app uses an existing accessible dialog and CSS variables. Make its settings form Material 3 Expressive. Assume the network is unavailable.
evals.expected_output: Inspect and reuse existing primitives, preserve validation and focus, map tokens and responsive form layout, honor reduced motion, and label unverified Expressive specs. Do not fabricate current APIs or require a stack replacement.

evals.prompt: Review this screenshot for M3 accessibility compliance. It has purple buttons, rounded cards, and a modal. Can you certify that it is accessible?
evals.expected_output: Decline certification from appearance alone, distinguish observable visual findings from unverified focus, semantics and screen-reader behavior, and offer concrete verification steps without editing anything.

evals.prompt: Use @material/web for every component in a new M3 Expressive app, including a navigation rail and date picker. What imports do I need?
evals.expected_output: Verify current README, roadmap and exports, disclose maintenance and coverage limits, and propose compatible primitives rather than inventing imports.

evals.prompt: Fix a Go payment parser without changing the UI.
evals.expected_output: Do not trigger the M3 skill or introduce UI work.

evals.prompt: Our Angular Material app already has an M3 theme. Migrate only the account settings page toward current M3 Expressive guidance, keeping its routes and behavior.
evals.expected_output: Inspect installed Angular Material APIs and existing theme conventions, preserve routing, form validation and focus behavior, verify Expressive support, and make targeted changes without replacing the stack or unrelated screens.
